result.summary: Adds Cap'n Proto serialization and interface wrappers for interfaces::Chain and interfaces::Handler in the IPC subsystem. Updates the libmultiprocess subtree to support non-UNIX platforms and recent fixes. Exposes makeChain over IPC to allow out-of-process clients to invoke chain queries and receive block and chainstate notifications.
result.problem: The wallet and external clients cannot run as separate processes because there is no IPC mechanism to call Chain interface methods or receive asynchronous chain notifications from bitcoin-node.

open_concerns: Calling getBlockHash with out-of-bounds height causes node assertion failure in ChainImpl rather than returning an error (zaidmstrr).
General question on how interface methods should handle invalid or null parameters passed by non-C++ IPC clients (willcl-ark).
Broader architectural discussion on whether to expose raw existing interfaces or craft specialized IPC interfaces (Sjors, #34981).
resolved_concerns: Various type mismatches, missing struct fields (such as best_height in estimateSmartFee), and signedness differences caught during review were fixed in rebases (l0rinc, sedited).
Client disconnect crashes during node shutdown investigated and tracked upstream in libmultiprocess (darosior, sedited, ryanofsky).

result.card: This pull request defines Cap'n Proto messages and wrappers to expose interfaces::Chain and interfaces::Handler over IPC sockets. It directly addresses the lack of out-of-process access to node chainstate, serving as the required dependency for running the Bitcoin Core wallet out of process in #10102. Several developers have validated the interface against independent external applications, including a Rust BDK wallet and an Electrs integration. Review state is active and ready, with strong support and no blocking objections.
